newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to meet Clinton in early 1997 - Kremlin.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to meet Clinton in early 1997 - Kremlin.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin plans to meet U.S. President Bill Clinton in the first half of 1997, the Kremlin said on Tuesday.
A Kremlin spokesman said the two leaders had agreed on the meeting on Monday after U.S. Vice President Al Gore and Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin met in Lisbon.

But the Kremlin said the two men had still not chosen the exact place or date for the encounter. The presidential press office said Yeltsin felt a meeting would be timely because both men had been re-elected to second terms in 1996.

The presidents last met in April in Moscow during a summit on nuclear safety. Yeltsin is recovering from multiple bypass heart surgery carried out almost a month ago and has resumed a light work schedule.
